title: Research
text:
Current research projects:
- Development of biological age clocks:
We are developing biological age clocks using the omics data (e.g. metabolomics and epigenomics) from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA). We are utilizing machine learning methods to develop metabolomic age based on the metabolomics data and multi-omics age by integrating metabolomics and epigenomics data.
Funding:
We received funding of $68,016 from the Canadian Institute of Health Research (CIHR) for this project.
Publications/Presentations:
Development of metabolomics age clock and identification of important metabolites. Annual International Conference of the Metabolomics Society, Japan, June 16-20, 2024
- Prediction of fragility fracture:
We are developing a machine learning algorithm to predict the fragility fracture using the data from the Canadian Multi-centre Osteoporosis Study (CaMos). We are also performing SHAP analysis to identify the important features and their interactions.
Funding:
We received funding of $20,000 from Osteoporosis Canada through the OC-CaMos fellowship for this project.
Publications/Presentations:
Prediction of Fragility Fracture and Identification of Important Factors – an Interpretable Machine Learning Approach. Annual Meeting of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research (ASBMR), Toronto, Canada, September 27-30, 2024.
- Role of genetics on frailty and sarcopenia:
We are investigating both standard statistical methods and machine learning methods for genome-wide association study for frailty and sarcopenia using the genetics data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA).

title: Sayem Borhan, PhD
text:
Hello, thank you for visiting my page.
I am an academic biostatistician and health researcher with a strong background in health research methods, biostatistics, and data science. I have extensive experience, expertise, and skills in designing and conducting health research studies.
I am involved in both methodological and epidemiological research. My research areas include clinical trials, real-world evidence, causal inference, omics, systematic review and meta-analysis, data science, machine learning, aging and bone health. I am also interested in collaborative research.
I work as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Health Research Methods, Evidence, and Impact (HEI) at McMaster University and as a methodologist/biostatistician at the Research Institute of St Joseph’s Healthcare Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.

title: Consultancy
text: I am involved in biostatistical consulting for health research, assisting academic and industry partners with methodological design and statistical analysis. My services cover a range of study types, including randomized controlled trials, machine learning, pilot studies, observational studies, and systematic reviews/meta-analyses. For collaboration and consultancy, please contact me.

title: Teaching
text:
I am involve in teaching in the Health Research Methodology (HRM) graduate program in the Department of Health Research Methods, Evidence, and Impact (HEI). Currently contributing to the following courses:

HRM 707: Advanced Epideiologic Methods
HRM 702: Introduction to Biostatistics
HRM 750: Practical Bayesian Design and Analysis in Clinical Studies
